decisions_log.decision: tick read path under a zero-scan budget
options_considered: scan filtered_trades with a manifest join
decisions_log.why: The first two both require a full pass over the 4.95B-row filtered_trades (no index exists), which is escalation row 4. Folder reads are genuinely targeted. Licensed by proving equivalence rather than assuming it: 56/56 dev v4 events, 9,638,361 rows, exactly equal to filtered_trades_dev_v4, which was itself materialized from filtered_trades.

decisions_log.decision: stratification variable for the extension draw
decisions_log.why: momentum_pct is a completed-day PRICE-move stratifier and is the axis dev v4 primary was already drawn on, so reusing it samples one axis twice and leaves session activity uncontrolled. T1 asks that the cohort span the range of session activity; T=0 print count IS session activity, is tick-derived (D4-clean), and spans four orders of magnitude across D1 (p01 135, median 21,585, max 4,856,965).

pybursts is not installed in the project .venv and installing an unpinned package mid-phase is worse than a ~40-line auditable implementation of a fully specified algorithm; no R toolchain is available. Verified against brute-force enumeration of all 2^5 state paths on 200 randomized quiet-burst-quiet trials, plus burst index-resolution cases.

options_considered: interval Jaccard on the union of burst intervals
decisions_log.chose: interval Jaccard primary; burst-count agreement reported alongside
decisions_log.why: The downstream use of this phase is burst-relative ANCHORING, so what matters is whether the same REGIONS of the session get labeled. Count agreement can be perfect while intervals sit elsewhere entirely, and poor while the same region is labeled with one extra split. Both are reported; only Jaccard is the failure-row-3 statistic.

options_considered: only sessions the canonical trades_bitmap marks collected
decisions_log.chose: collected per trades_bitmap, falling back to print presence only where the bitmap is NULL
decisions_log.why: A COLLECTED session with zero prints is real information (the name did not trade) and must contribute zero-count minute slots; an UNCOLLECTED session must contribute nothing rather than silently pulling the baseline toward zero. Used on 114/114 cohort events.

The prompt requires the directory be gitignored per §12, but the repo-root .gitignore is outside the escalation-row-7 write allowlist. A nested file achieves the §12 outcome (446 MB of regenerable HTML stays untracked) with every write inside the allowlist.

decisions_log.decision: row_cap_census added as a fourth cohort group
options_considered: report the observed zero and move on
force-include all 8 D1 row-cap events as a never-pooled census
decisions_log.chose: never-pooled census, added at T1 before any measurement ran
decisions_log.why: The seeded extension draw returned 0 of the 8 D1 row-cap events (8/15,763; a 100-event draw catches one ~5% of the time), so the prompt's requirement that flagged events be 'carried, labeled and reported as their own row throughout' had nothing to report on. Same construction the dev v4 sidecar already uses. Cannot move a headline number because it is never pooled; the seeded draw is unchanged.

Arm A's reference burst duration median is 2.39s, so at the original grid's first point (5s) every Arm A burst was already terminal and its curve was pinned at 1.0 across the whole axis — chart 06 could not display the arm it exists to describe. Display-resolution change only: adds sample points to an existing curve, touches no threshold, parameter, segmentation or pre-registered criterion.

surprises: The cohort draw was not actually reproducible as first written. The stratification decile used rank(method="first") over a DataFrame whose row order came from a SELECT with no ORDER BY, so tied t0_print_count values landed in different deciles on different runs and the seeded draw silently returned different events (an earlier run drew DPRO 2024-04-01 and IMTE 2023-10-27; a later one did not). Caught only because stale burst rows failed to join at T6b. The in-run reproducibility check did not catch it because it compared two draws off the same in-memory pool. Fixed by sorting before ranking; the check now rebuilds the decile from row-shuffled inputs, so it tests order-independence rather than repeatability. Any phase drawing a stratified sample in pandas off an unordered SQL read has this exposure.

Arm B read `trades_bitmap` via getattr(row, ..., None) and the column was never selected into the cohort manifest, so all 114 events silently used the print-presence fallback while config documented the bitmap rule. A defaulted getattr turned a schema gap into a quiet method downgrade; it now raises.

The two arms are close to uncorrelated on burst count: Spearman -0.216, and burst-count agreement is 0/100 events. Arm A returns more bursts on 67/100 events, Arm B on 33/100. Median interval Jaccard 0.307.

Arm A's median burst duration is 2.39s and its median time-to-burst-high is 0.117s, with 25% of bursts taking their high on the burst's first print. Arm A's timescale sits two orders of magnitude below Arm B's on every one of duration, spacing and time-to-high.

The row-cap census splits the two arms in opposite directions: Arm A returns MORE bursts on capped events (median 395 vs 98.5 pooled) while Arm B returns FEWER (median 5.5 vs 25.0 pooled). All 8 capped events terminate at exactly 50,000 / 100,000 / 200,000 prints, so the session tail is absent by construction.

82 of 114 cohort events are baseline_partial — at least one in-window minute-of-session has no flanking print in its +/-15 minute neighbourhood. Only 32 are fully defined. 1 (RBC 2022-09-26, sidecar) is baseline_undefined with 0 collected flanking sessions.
8,197,948 cohort prints fall outside the extended-day [04:00, 20:00) window across the 4 sessions read and are excluded from segmentation by the D3 clock.
